name: Uokha
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page uokh1238 'Uokha' (Bookkeeping; 'Merged into Emai-Iuleha-Ora [ema]' via CR 2014-043).
sources.note: No references of its own (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology apart from the ISO change request); confirms retired status.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 1994. Emai verbal and preverbal tone: preliminaries. Paper, 25th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, New Brunswick. ERIC document ED375640, 16 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 2: Emai 'manifests two significant level tones low and high, but permits rising and falling tone to emerge when the former are syntactically juxtaposed'; verbs, auxiliaries and preverbs get tone by rule. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur in the text (only 'accent' in a reference title).

sources.citation: Rüdiger Köppe Verlag publisher page for A Dictionary of Emai (koeppe.de/titel_a-dictionary-of-emai).
sources.note: Blurb: sketch covers orthography and pronunciation, word classes, clause structure and 'tonal variations'; no sample pages.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2022. Secondary concepts and internal dynamics of Emai Serial Verb Constructions. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 65: 233-265. doi:10.5842/65-1-976
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 234: 'A tonal language, Emai shows lexical and grammatical tones high, low, and downstep high'; verbs lexically toneless, toneme suffixes spread. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2014. Change Request Number 2014-043: adopted merge [uok] into [ema], adopted update [ema] (2015-01-12). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity only: 'Uokha [uok] is a place name where the language of the clans Emai, Iuleha and Ora is spoken (Elugbe 1989:22-24, Jungraithmayr and Ganslmayr 1986:34), but this language already is already included in Emai-Iuleha-Ora [ema]' (p. 2, 4b).

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan. Ibadan University Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Read only the Uokha passages (pp. 67-69 region of the scanned): Elugbe 1989 left the lects of Ihievbe, Ivbiaro, Warrake, Era, Uokha, Atte, Enwa, Ososo unclassified; 'Oyakhire (1997) confirms this when he defines the following dialect groups: A: Emai, Ihievbe, Ora, Iuleha, Ievbu, Uokha, Urore, Ohami, Sobe.' Oral-tradition tapes were recorded at Uokha. Nothing on stress in these passages.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Uokha language' (redirects to 'Ivbiosakon language' = Emai-Iuleha-Ora; cites Ethnologue 18, Glottolog, Archangeli & Pulleyblank 1994, Mielke 2008).
sources.note: Only Aoma-dialect segmental inventory (7 vowels in two harmonic sets; one phonemic nasal /m/); nothing on tone or stress; does not name Uokha among the dialects.

sources.citation: Donwa-Ifode, Shirley O. 1990. Transitional phonologies and their implication for orthographies: the case of Ora. Journal of West African Languages 20(2): 3-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned text we hold for stress/accent/prominence: no hits (the earlier emai1241 reader records it as a segmental sketch of Ora with tone only in the genitival floating-H discussion, pp. 15-16). The one Ora-lect phonology; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2017. A grammar of Emai (Mouton Grammar Library 72). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Chapter 1 'Orthography and grammatical overview', pp. 1-20 (§1.3 Tone and orthography, §1.4 Syllable structure, pronunciation and orthography, §1.5 Basic sentence types and pitch register).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only full modern reference grammar of the language; its phonology overview is where any statement on stress vs. tone, or on the absence of word stress, would be made.

sources.citation: Lewis, Ademola Anthony. 2013. North Edoid relations and roots. PhD dissertation, University of Ibadan. xvi+327 pp. (Glottolog ref 550315)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Modern comparative treatment of the North Edoid (Owan) lects, the only recent work likely to include Uokha-area data; could settle whether any Owan lect shows non-tonal prominence.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2007. A dictionary of Emai: an Edoid language of Nigeria, including a grammatical sketch (Westafrikanische Studien 32). Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. Grammatical sketch §2.3 'Tonal features' and §3 'Syllables, word classes and pronunciation'.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not downloaded; only the abstract or a snippet was reachable when a reader tried
sources.note: First-hand sketch with tone and pronunciation sections; full-text search shows 'stress' absent, so it would document the silence and give the tonal description in full. Readable with a free archive.org borrow (id dictionaryofemai00scha); PDF also sold by the publisher.

sources.citation: Oyakhire, [initials unknown]. 1997. [Dialect survey of the Owan/North Edoid lects; title not recovered], cited in Egbokhare 2011: 68 for dialect group A (Emai, Ihievbe, Ora, Iuleha, Ievbu, Uokha, Urore, Ohami, Sobe).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The one work known to have surveyed Uokha as a lect; probably an Ibadan thesis with wordlists and perhaps prosodic notes. Bibliographic details not recoverable from the scanned of Egbokhare 2011.

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Oisaghaede Francis. 1990. A phonology of Emai. PhD dissertation, University of Ibadan. xvii+396 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The dedicated phonology of the Emai lect (source of the Emai data in Archangeli & Pulleyblank 1994); most likely place for an explicit remark on stress/accent and syllable prominence. Not in the UI repository.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: phonology and lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press. (pp. 22-24 on Uokha per ISO CR 2014-043)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The Edoid comparative phonology that classifies Uokha within Ora-Emai-Iuleha; its phonology chapters would state the prosodic type (tone; any accent) for the family and may carry Uokha wordlist data.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben O. 1989. Edoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America. archive.org id nigercongolangua0000unse (lending-only).
